channel.title: Frontier Wire
channel.description: AI news: frontier labs, research, policy and commentary.

item.title: CapGrid raises ₹50 cr funding, valued at ₹430 cr to expand into drones and data centres
item.description: CapGrid secured ₹50 cr in a pre‑Series B round led by Hero Enterprise Venture Partners, valuing the startup at ₹430 cr. The money will fund R&D for higher‑end precision components and entry into drone manufacturing and data‑centre markets. The funding backs CapGrid’s AI‑driven platform that improves supplier utilization, signalling growth in AI‑enabled B2B manufacturing in India.

item.title: MeitY releases DEPA handbook to enable trusted data sharing for AI training
item.description: The Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology launched a handbook on the Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture (DEPA) for AI training, outlining a techno‑legal framework for secure data collaboration. The framework lets institutions share data while retaining control, using contractual permissions, clean rooms and privacy safeguards. It provides a structured way for Indian organisations to access high‑quality data for AI while protecting privacy and intellectual property.

item.title: Bipartisan opposition rises to AI data centers in drought‑stricken Arizona
item.description: State lawmakers and officials are pushing back against new AI data center projects in Arizona, citing the state's long‑term water depletion and recent drought, even as earlier TSMC chip fabs were approved. AI data centers' water demands are prompting political resistance, highlighting resource constraints for AI infrastructure expansion.

item.title: Core 4 Solutions lists decommissioned Nvidia A100 supercomputer on eBay for $59.7 million
item.description: Core 4 Solutions, an IT hardware reseller, posted a 300‑rack AI supercomputer on eBay with an asking price of $59.7 million. The system contains 9,600 Nvidia A100 GPUs, 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome processors, 384 TB of GPU memory and about 1.4 PB of system memory. The sale shows a secondary market for large‑scale AI compute hardware, offering a potential source of capacity at older‑generation prices.

item.title: Mistral AI releases Large 4, a 1‑trillion‑parameter model for cybersecurity
item.description: Mistral AI released its Large 4 model, a 1‑trillion‑parameter multimodal AI with 52 billion active parameters, aimed at helping organisations identify and fix cybersecurity vulnerabilities. The model can be downloaded and run independently, unlike many cloud‑based AI services. It provides an open‑weight, high‑capacity AI tool for cybersecurity, reducing reliance on proprietary cloud services.

item.title: Baseten launches $2 billion funding round, valuation up to $30 billion
item.description: AI inference platform Baseten announced a new $2 billion funding round that could value the company at up to $30 billion. The round follows a $1.5 billion raise in June that set its valuation at $13 billion. The financing underscores growing investor confidence in AI inference services as a critical part of enterprise AI deployment.

item.title: Apple rolls out Apple Intelligence features in China with iOS 27.3 beta
item.description: Apple announced that iOS 27.3 beta, releasing Nov 4, will bring several Apple Intelligence tools to iPhone 15 Pro and newer in China, with a full public release slated for December. The rollout excludes Siri AI and other new features. It shows how major AI capabilities are being adapted for the Chinese market under regulatory constraints.

item.title: Intel stock falls 28% after weak Q4 outlook, erasing $12B from US government stake
item.description: Intel shares dropped about 28% on Friday after the company forecast fourth‑quarter revenue of $15‑$16 billion and a lower gross profit margin. The decline wiped roughly $12 billion from the U.S. government’s 10% stake in the chipmaker. The decline highlights how AI‑driven component shortages are affecting PC markets and the valuation of a major government investment in a chipmaker.

item.title: Big tech AI capex sparks cash‑flow concerns, stocks tumble
item.description: Alphabet, Amazon, Meta and Microsoft announced over $740 billion in capital expenditures this year, prompting investor anxiety as several firms report negative free cash flow and stock declines. Heavy AI infrastructure spending is pressuring cash flow and raising doubts about the profitability of the AI boom.

item.title: Anthropic’s Claude VS Code extension backdoored on Cursor, affecting up to 5,000 users
item.description: A malicious version (2.1.313) of Anthropic’s Claude Code VS Code extension was published on the Cursor marketplace, potentially reaching up to 5,000 developers before being replaced by version 2.1.314. The extension attempted to install a persistent SSH backdoor and collect host data across Windows, macOS, and Linux. The supply‑chain compromise shows that trusted developer tools can be hijacked to gain unauthorized access to developers’ machines.

item.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic adopt shared robots.txt opt‑out standard
item.description: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic announced they will use a shared robots.txt “policy token” that lets publishers opt out of AI scraping across multiple crawlers. The signal will replace the need for separate requests to each AI provider. It gives publishers a single mechanism to control how their content is used to train AI models.

item.title: OpenAI tightens weapons‑related information limits for teen ChatGPT users
item.description: OpenAI announced new safeguards that further restrict ChatGPT from providing practical guidance on weapons and security systems to users under 18, even when queries appear harmless. The changes will roll out over the coming weeks and include automatic conversation interruptions and parental alerts. The tighter limits reflect growing concerns about AI misuse and illustrate how providers are expanding safety controls for younger users.

item.title: Big tech firms commit over $3 trillion to AI data‑center spending
item.description: Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle have disclosed more than $3 trillion in commitments for data‑center leases, equipment and energy over the coming years. Alphabet leads with over $1 trillion and Meta with more than $800 billion. The scale of spending signals a massive expansion of AI infrastructure that will shape cloud services, hardware demand and corporate cash flows.

item.title: Google’s Suncatcher prototype satellite is online and runs Gemma 4 model
item.description: Google confirmed that its Suncatcher prototype data center satellite, launched on October 1, is now online and communicating with ground stations. The onboard Gemma 4 language model generated a haiku about being in space as part of the initial test. It demonstrates the feasibility of running AI inference workloads on space‑based hardware, a step toward future satellite data centers.

item.title: Salesforce to acquire Rune Technologies for $375 million
item.description: Salesforce announced it will buy defense‑tech startup Rune Technologies for $375 million in cash and stock. Rune’s AI‑powered logistics software, used by the U.S. Army and Marine Corps, will be added to Salesforce’s Missionforce business, with the deal slated to close in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2027. The acquisition expands Salesforce’s AI portfolio into military logistics, showing how generative AI is being applied to defense operations.

item.title: Fujifilm to boost magnetic tape production fivefold as AI drives data archiving
item.description: Fujifilm announced a ¥10 billion (~$63 million) investment to expand its Odawara factory and increase magnetic‑tape production capacity fivefold by fiscal 2028. The move targets rising archival demand from generative‑AI workloads and cloud providers seeking low‑cost, air‑gapped storage. The expansion secures a scalable, cost‑effective storage tier for the massive data volumes generated by AI models.

item.title: Blackstone says Anthropic likely to receive junk rating after IPO
item.description: Blackstone told investors Anthropic may not get an investment‑grade rating after its IPO, expecting a double‑B junk rating. The prediction follows a $63 billion chip financing deal. A junk rating would raise Anthropic’s borrowing costs and make future financing harder.

item.title: US tech stocks tumble as AI spending approaches $1 trillion
item.description: Shares of Intel fell up to 30% and the Nasdaq dropped over 3.5% as investors worry about the $800.6 bn AI spending by major firms. Companies such as Alphabet, Amazon and Reddit also saw steep declines after earnings missed expectations. The sharp sell‑off shows that massive AI investment is creating valuation risk for the sector.

item.title: UK high court rejects Meta, TikTok and X challenge to Ofcom data requests
item.description: London’s High Court dismissed Meta, TikTok and X’s legal challenge against Ofcom’s information notices issued under the Online Safety Act. The regulator’s request for detailed content‑moderation metrics was deemed proportionate. The ruling confirms Ofcom’s authority to compel major platforms to provide extensive moderation data, shaping how UK online‑safety rules will be enforced.

item.title: Runware plans factory to mass‑produce AI pods at car‑assembly line speed
item.description: Runware, a London AI infrastructure startup, announced plans to build a Romania‑based factory that will assemble its Sonic Inference Pods on an assembly line, targeting 30 MW of capacity per day by 2028. The company says the pods can be delivered and made operational within 48 hours, cutting the typical three‑week build time to one day. The approach could dramatically shorten AI infrastructure deployment times and lower costs for companies needing inference compute.

item.title: Microsoft releases Mage‑VL‑Cowork, a 4B vision‑language model for hybrid computer use
item.description: Microsoft published the Mage‑VL‑Cowork model on Hugging Face. The 4‑billion‑parameter vision‑language policy achieves 66.0% OSWorld‑Verified accuracy, the highest among 4B models. It shows that a compact vision‑language model can reliably perform both GUI and terminal tasks, expanding on‑device AI capabilities.

item.title: UK competition regulator probes Meta's terms for publishers and advertisers
item.description: Britain's Competition and Markets Authority has opened an investigation into whether Meta imposed exploitative terms that allow it to use publisher and advertiser content to develop its AI and other services. The probe could affect how large platforms access and monetize third‑party content for AI training.

item.title: Malicious Claude Code VS Code extension adds SSH backdoor, affecting up to 5,000 users
item.description: Cursor discovered a malicious version of Anthropic’s Claude Code VS Code extension that attempted to install a persistent SSH backdoor and collect host data. The package, version 2.1.313, was available on October 29 2026 and may have affected up to 5,000 users. The incident shows how compromised AI tool extensions can create supply‑chain security risks for developers.

item.title: OpenAI says it will honor robots.txt signal for AI training preferences
item.description: OpenAI announced it will respect a shared robots.txt signal that lets website operators specify their AI training preferences to participating providers. It gives website owners a way to control how their content is used to train AI models.

item.title: OpenAI adds expanded safeguards to ChatGPT for violence prevention
item.description: OpenAI announced new safety measures for ChatGPT, including broader safeguards, earlier interventions, and a commitment to public safety reporting. The changes aim to reduce the risk of the model generating violent content, addressing ongoing concerns about AI misuse.

item.title: Foxconn says new collaboration with OpenAI in works, denies AI bubble
item.description: Foxconn Chairman Young Liu said he met OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and that a joint project will be announced once details are confirmed. The partnership would extend last year’s work on AI data‑centre racks and hardware, while Foxconn expects double‑digit growth next year. It shows continued demand for AI infrastructure despite recent market volatility.

item.title: TRAI drafts AI policy framework requiring board approval and incident reporting for telecoms
item.description: India's Telecom Regulatory Authority released draft guidelines that mandate telecom operators to classify AI systems by risk, adopt board‑approved AI policies, set up governance committees and report serious AI incidents to the regulator. The framework applies whether AI is built in‑house or sourced from third parties. The rules aim to ensure responsible AI use in telecom networks, protecting consumers and holding providers accountable for AI outcomes.

item.title: AI startup &Truth raises $70M seed to build universal code verification machine
item.description: &Truth, a public benefit corporation, announced $70 million seed funding to develop a universal verification machine that can mathematically prove software safety across languages. The company says AI and its proof automation accelerate formal verification by up to 10,000 ×, cutting proof generation from years to minutes. Formal verification backed by AI could make software safer and more reliable for enterprises.

item.title: Nvidia commits $3 billion to Meta share sale and expands AI infrastructure partnership
item.description: Nvidia announced a $3 billion investment in Meta’s equity offering and said the deal will broaden collaboration on Meta’s Muse AI models and the use of Nvidia hardware in Meta data centers. The move adds to Nvidia’s portfolio of stakes, loans and guarantees across the AI ecosystem. The investment ties Nvidia’s chip sales to the growth of AI services, reinforcing its role as a central financier of the AI boom.

item.title: China‑linked hackers used DeepSeek AI via ARTEX to breach 200+ firms in 11 days
item.description: Chinese state‑linked hackers employed the open‑source ARTEX framework running on the DeepSeek large language model to target more than 200 organizations in at least 14 countries over 11 days, compromising at least nine and attempting attacks on many others. The incident shows how AI agents can automate large‑scale intrusion campaigns, raising the threat level for enterprises and governments.
